The print has بكل, not لكل. The predicate of the second hemistich is supplied from the first (love), not a literal copula “am”; the explanatory note explicitly confirms this interpretation. Its attribution to Ibn al-Farid is reported by this edition, not independently established here.

Both occurrences use عرض, not فرض. Maintain distinction between existence itself and derivative attribution; do not turn this into denial of every relation of dependence.

The print corroborates the glass/ray construction and reads فتراءى, but does not independently justify replacing للزجاج with a different preposition. Do not certify the older English through as a literal counterpart. No independent poetic attribution is established.
records.followUp: The glass/ray phrase is intelligible with the printed للزجاج; render radiance appearing in the glass, not as an asserted literal through.

records.decision: The complete opening quoted commentary is visible. Bracketed modern clarifications are excluded from the proposed medieval reading.
The printed quotation supplies ظاهر العلم, absent/disordered in the electronic string. This is a technical relational account, not the bare definition “possibility is existence”.
The print distinguishes عدم الاستحقاقية (absence of entitlement) from استحقاقية العدم (entitlement to nonbeing). The latter, not the former, belongs in this counterfactual.
The complete quoted passage contains one dependent-nature statement; the adjacent electronic repeat is absent.
The print has no following لا عن مرتبة الاسم الظاهر. Removing the redundant contradictory tail restores the stated Hidden/Manifest contrast.

The quotation runs across the page boundary once; the shorter duplicate فله المطلق في الحدوث والقدم is absent. This is Ibn Arabi quoted within Ibn Turka, not a separately collated edition of Insha al-Dawair.
النهي is explicit in the printed quoted commentary; the previous النسى is not retained as an unexplained technical word.
The physical account is the historical argument being reported. H2014 prints the clause once, without the electronic repetition of لا بد وأن يكون عرضاً جسمانياً وذلك لأن الرؤية.
The negative لا is explicitly printed in the quoted medieval passage. The source-supported correction restores the dialectical voice, not merely smoother English.
The printed faculty list reads الفكرية, not the digital الكفرية.
